name: CH340G
description: Low-cost USB 2.0 full-speed to UART bridge widely used on inexpensive serial adapters and Arduino clones. It emulates a standard serial port and provides the common modem-control signals (RTS, DTR, DCD, RI, DSR, CTS), supporting 50 bps to 2 Mbps. The G variant in SOP-16 requires an external 12 MHz crystal on XI/XO; it runs from 5 V or 3.3 V and is software-compatible with the CH341 driver. Cheap and ubiquitous, though it relies on the vendor (WCH) VCP driver rather than a class driver.

pins.name: V3
pins.description: regulator pin: 100 nF decoupling cap to GND when VCC=5 V; tie to VCC when running at 3.3 V

pins.name: UD+
pins.description: USB D+ (connect directly to USB, no external resistor)

pins.name: UD-
pins.description: USB D- (connect directly to USB, no external resistor)

pins.name: CTS#
pins.description: clear to send modem input (active low)

pins.name: DSR#
pins.description: data set ready modem input (active low)

pins.name: DCD#
pins.description: data carrier detect modem input (active low)

pins.name: DTR#
pins.description: data terminal ready modem output (active low)

pins.name: RTS#
pins.description: request to send modem output (active low)

pins.name: R232
pins.description: RS-232 enable / signal-inversion control; normally left unconnected (low) for standard TTL polarity

extra.Vcc: 5V mode: 4.5-5.3V (V3 not tied to VCC). 3.3V mode: 3.3-3.8V (V3 tied to VCC). Abs max VCC: -0.5 to 6.5V
extra.clock: external 12 MHz crystal on G variant (XI/XO)

typical_application: USB-to-TTL-serial adapter and on-board USB programming/console interface for microcontroller boards.
gotchas: CH340G needs an external 12 MHz crystal across XI (pin 7) and XO (pin 8) - the C/E/N/K/X/B variants have a built-in clock and need no crystal
V3 (pin 4) is a regulator pin: add a 100 nF cap to GND for 5 V operation, but tie V3 to VCC for 3.3 V operation
requires the WCH driver; older OS driver versions are buggy and many fake/older driver binaries float around - use a current WCH driver
the variants come in different packages (CH340G/C/B SOP-16, CH340N SOP-8, CH340E/X MSOP-10, CH340K ESSOP-10, CH340T/R SSOP-20) - pinouts differ, do not assume
UD+/UD- connect straight to the USB connector; WCH explicitly says do NOT add series/pull-up resistors on the data lines
for auto-reset on Arduino-style boards, DTR#/RTS# are wired through a capacitor to the MCU reset/DTR line
